responseText: {"title":"Pressure and Containment","question":"What happens when a face or figure seems to be held in—or bursting out of—its own boundaries?","introduction":"Twenty works, each built around a head or skull, line these walls. In every one, outlines press inward while interior marks push back. Teeth, frames, bands, rings, and bolted visors recur as both structure and subject. The exhibition asks you to watch where the boundary holds, where it strains, and whether containment reads as protection or as trap.","closing":"Each work draws its own edge and then tests it. Whether that edge reads as shelter or as cage may depend less on the marks than on the moment you look.","chapters":[{"title":"Faces That Float","introduction":"Four heads presented against flat, unbroken grounds. The outline is the only thing separating figure from field—and it is already under pressure from within.","stops":[{"slot":"W001","whyHere":"A translucent, swollen head floats on an unbroken red field; its outline barely contains pooling color patches and mismatched yellow eyes.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W061","whyHere":"A heavy black outline holds a head crammed with multicolored scrawl against a clean blue ground; one eye catches a pinpoint of light, the other is hollow.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both heads float on flat single-color grounds, but where W001's outline is soft and translucent, this one is a thick black wall barely containing the wiring inside."},{"slot":"W047","whyHere":"On a saturated magenta field, dense black strokes build a face that collapses depth into a flat, pressing confrontation with no breathing room.","transitionFromPrevious":"The clean blue ground gives way to an all-over magenta that eliminates any sense of distance, pushing the face forward with nowhere to recede."},{"slot":"W030","whyHere":"A head emerges from a hot orange field as flat black fragments and wire-like outlines; a teal X in the eye area reads as something refused or sealed off.","transitionFromPrevious":"The magenta field is replaced by a warm orange, but the same flatness persists—here the face fragments rather than consolidates, its eye crossed out rather than staring."}]},{"title":"Marks That Multiply","introduction":"Works where the interior of the face is so densely layered that the marks themselves become a second kind of boundary—a cage built from scribble.","stops":[{"slot":"W002","whyHere":"Yellow loops, teal tangles, and a jaw broken open by sharp white teeth build a head that vibrates against its still purple ground.","transitionFromPrevious":"Moving from a fragmented orange face to a purple ground, the marks here multiply into a dense crown that feels like a shout caught mid-release."},{"slot":"W006","whyHere":"Dense interior hatching makes this animal-like head feel caged inside its own lines; teal peeks through gaps in the black scaffolding.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works pile marks until the face feels trapped inside them, but where W002 erupts upward, this one turns inward, its whisker-lines pressing against the frame."},{"slot":"W016","whyHere":"Jagged white teeth appear everywhere—around eyes, across the brow, lining the mouth—so the whole head reads as a structure built from biting.","transitionFromPrevious":"The animal silhouette of W006 gives way to a more frontal face, but the tooth motif spreads from mouth to every border, turning the whole surface into a biting edge."},{"slot":"W029","whyHere":"The face splits almost down its center—yellow and blue marks flood the left, red and teal claim the right—holding two moods in one skull.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W016 repeats one motif across the whole face, this head divides itself, its dense marks segregated into two competing halves."},{"slot":"W034","whyHere":"Thick black scribbles press the face inward against a muted brown ground; two eye circles fringed with fang marks watch from a compressed, lopsided skull.","transitionFromPrevious":"The split face of W029 is replaced by a face that feels compressed from all sides, its scrawl so dense the head seems to be shrinking under its own marks."}]},{"title":"Frames Within Faces","introduction":"Works where a geometric structure—rectangle, grid, nested box, or band—appears inside or around the face, adding a second layer of enclosure.","stops":[{"slot":"W004","whyHere":"A skull sits frontal on saturated blue; eye circles contain layered spirals and grids, and a dark grid of thin lines crosses the upper background.","transitionFromPrevious":"The compressed brown face opens onto a bright blue field, but the skull's eye sockets now contain their own internal grids, enclosure folded inside enclosure."},{"slot":"W012","whyHere":"A rectangular barred socket at the face's center suggests something sealed behind the surface; gold teeth flash against a dark mouth cavity like ornament and lock at once.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W004's grids sit inside the eyes, here a single barred rectangle dominates the face's center, reading unmistakably as a window with bars."},{"slot":"W044","whyHere":"Yellow banding runs across chin, cheeks, and forehead, striping the face like a crate; two eyes carry different internal marks—zigzag versus cross—lending asymmetric unease.","transitionFromPrevious":"The barred socket of W012 gives way to horizontal banding that wraps the whole face, turning the head into a striped, boxed form."},{"slot":"W055","whyHere":"Teal bars stack along one edge while vertical stripes press the other; crossed-out eyes and a red triangle crown give the boxed-in head a confrontational, almost comic charge.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both works use banding to press the face inward, but here the bands migrate to the margins, squeezing the head from outside rather than marking it from within."},{"slot":"W010","whyHere":"Concentric nested rectangles pull the eye toward a tight spiral at the center; sawtooth lines slice across the surface like static, with barely any negative space surviving.","transitionFromPrevious":"The banded face gives way to a composition where the frame is the entire subject—nested rectangles with no face at all, containment stripped to its purest geometry."},{"slot":"W048","whyHere":"Thick black borders stack and lean like crates; a red spiral anchors the upper center while a zigzag band cuts the lower third, resisting any single focal point.","transitionFromPrevious":"W010's concentric inward pull is answered here by angular boxes that lean and collide, replacing centered compression with a restless, multi-directional push."}]},{"title":"Skulls and Their Ornaments","introduction":"Skull forms that carry decorative additions—chains, medallions, visors, medallion-suns—where the ornament both adorns and further constrains the form.","stops":[{"slot":"W017","whyHere":"Red dashes burst outward behind the skull like a broadcast signal; teeth ring the eye sockets as well as the jaw, multiplying mouths across the whole face.","transitionFromPrevious":"Moving from abstract boxes back to a face, this skull radiates outward—the first work in the exhibition where the boundary seems to be pushing energy away rather than holding it in."},{"slot":"W051","whyHere":"A chain and medallion pull the skull rightward; radiating color bands fan behind it, making the form feel ornamental and hollow at once—festive and unsettling.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W017's skull broadcasts outward through red dashes, this one is weighted down by a chain, its outward radiation replaced by decorative gravity."},{"slot":"W054","whyHere":"Rectangular goggle-like eye shapes give the skull a mask quality; cyan and yellow patches leak through black scaffolding, suggesting a lit-from-within instability.","transitionFromPrevious":"The chain of W051 adds external weight; here the skull's own eye sockets become rigid rectangular frames, containment built into the anatomy itself."},{"slot":"W041","whyHere":"An oversized pink visor turns eyewear into a grinning mouth-border; a small dripping form at the jaw suggests something leaking out of an otherwise sealed figure.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where W054's rectangular eyes are hollow and stiff, this visor is pink and tooth-rimmed, transforming a protective object into a boundary that grins back."}]},{"title":"The Ring, the Split, the Stare","introduction":"Three works where the boundary takes a distinct visible form—a white ring, a divided skull, a ringed eye—and the question of armor versus trap becomes most direct.","stops":[{"slot":"W058","whyHere":"A heavy white ring frames a face staring through mismatched eyes; all pattern density is concentrated inside the circle, the surrounding field left sparse.","transitionFromPrevious":"The visor of W041 is a partial frame; here a complete white ring encloses the entire face, making the boundary a deliberate, visible object rather than an edge."},{"slot":"W047","whyHere":"Revisited here as a closing contrast: on its flat magenta field, the face has no ring, no chain, no visor—only the pressure of the ground itself as containment.","transitionFromPrevious":"The white ring of W058 makes containment explicit and geometric; this work strips it away entirely, leaving only color pressure as the boundary—the most invisible cage in the exhibition."},{"slot":"W061","whyHere":"The thick black outline barely holds colored scrawl; one eye dark, one catching a pinpoint of light; bared teeth too wide; an orange-red drop hangs from the chin, untouched by the surrounding blue.","transitionFromPrevious":"Against the magenta field's invisible pressure, this head returns to the explicit black outline of the exhibition's opening—but now the scrawl inside reads differently, as something that has been watching the whole time."}]}]}
